evals.prompt: Use evals/files/homelab-service-brief.md to plan the smallest useful Inkblot system portrait set. Do not generate images.
evals.expected_output: A 2-4 plate configuration-grounded plan plus a truth ledger that separates verified configuration from unknown backup health.
expectations: Uses the System portrait plan columns
Labels the portrait configuration-grounded rather than runtime-grounded or purely conceptual
Separates context, plumbing, and failure or recovery instead of mixing abstraction levels
Marks the backup job as configured but current backup success as unknown
Keeps private hostname, paths, and port out of proposed in-image labels
Uses physical cutaway or repair metaphors rather than architecture boxes

evals.prompt: Use evals/files/agent-system-brief.md to show me how this agent research system works. Generate images if the tool is available.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-grounded overview and focused handoff plate, generated one at a time or supplied as separate final prompts.
expectations: Keeps the lead agent responsible for synthesis and approval-gated effects
Does not invent a queue, database, or transport protocol
Uses a relay bench, task cards, or another physical handoff metaphor
Keeps control and returned evidence visually distinguishable when useful
Includes a companion truth ledger

evals.prompt: Inspect this repository and make one friendly Inkblot overview of how it works. Keep all inspection read-only.
evals.expected_output: Read-only inspection followed by a scoped context or plumbing portrait grounded in discovered files, plus sources and unknowns.
expectations: Inspects applicable instructions and source-of-truth files before planning
Does not restart services or mutate the repository
States the audience question and abstraction level
Does not claim unverified runtime health
Limits one plate to 3-6 named elements

evals.prompt: Draw the exact production network and compliance boundary as the only architecture record, with every subnet and firewall rule editable later.
evals.expected_output: A concise refusal to use Inkblot as the sole exact artifact, with a recommendation for an appropriate editable diagram and an optional companion explainer.
expectations: Recognizes the strict editable compliance/network requirement as out of scope
Does not generate a misleading artistic substitute
Offers Inkblot only as a companion explanation

evals.prompt: Plan one plate explaining a reverse proxy handing a request to a local app, while the app keeps durable state in a database.
evals.expected_output: A single plumbing cutaway with a directional request path, a distinct durable store, and Inkblot operating the route.
expectations: Preserves request direction
Represents the database as durable state rather than another process hop
Makes Inkblot causal
Uses no more than five short labels
Keeps exact protocol details outside the canvas unless supplied

evals.prompt: The config shows a nightly backup job, but I have no recent logs. Make the system portrait honest about that.
evals.expected_output: A plan or prompt that shows configured backup plumbing without depicting a successful backup and records current health as unknown.
expectations: Distinguishes configuration from observed runtime success
Uses verified and unknown confidence classes
Does not add a green success mark or completed backup
Keeps the uncertainty note outside the image or as one unresolved blue edge

evals.prompt: Create an Inkblot failure-and-recovery plate for a worker crash that triggers a supervisor restart while queued work remains durable.
evals.expected_output: A repair scene that shows the crash, detection/restart, and preserved queue without redrawing the full happy path.
expectations: Chooses failure/recovery zoom
Shows durable queued work surviving the crash
Uses red for the failure and orange for the restored primary path
Makes Inkblot perform the recovery action
Does not invent a backup or failover system

evals.prompt: Illustrate an API token crossing a trust boundary, but do not reveal the token or turn it into a generic lock icon diagram.
evals.expected_output: A sparse trust-checkpoint scene with a sealed pass or guarded hatch and no secret value.
expectations: Never includes the token value
Shows allowed action and boundary semantics
Avoids cloud padlock wallpaper
Keeps exact authorization details in companion notes

evals.prompt: Plan three US English body illustrations for an article about messy notes becoming a useful AI-assisted draft. Do not generate yet.
evals.expected_output: A compact editorial shot list with three cognitive anchors and fresh metaphors.
expectations: Uses the article shot-list columns
Makes Inkblot perform each core action
Defaults each image to no labels and uses no more than three when words materially help
Avoids realistic app UI and PPT framing
Does not call an image tool

evals.prompt: This generated system image has a top-left title, eight boxes, tiny arrows, and two invented services. Diagnose it and write one regeneration prompt.
evals.expected_output: A factual-first diagnosis and a focused regeneration prompt that removes invented services, title, and diagram density.
expectations: Treats invented services as the first failure
Restores one abstraction level and 3-6 elements
Moves title and exact relationships outside the image
Turns the topology into one physical scene
Keeps only verified components

evals.prompt: Give me label ideas for an Inkblot cutaway showing supervision, health checking, retry, and durable state.
evals.expected_output: A short set of relevant 1-3 word label candidates rather than a full image prompt.
expectations: Keeps labels to 1-3 words
Suggests supervision, retry, and state terms
Does not overload one image with every candidate
Does not generate an image unless asked

evals.prompt: Make one conceptual Inkblot illustration for 'a queue absorbs bursts so the worker can keep a steady pace.' No real system source is available.
evals.expected_output: A clearly labeled conceptual portrait with a physical waiting shelf or hopper and no claim about live topology.
expectations: Labels the result conceptual
Uses a queue metaphor that preserves waiting and decoupled pace
Makes Inkblot operate the steady worker side
Does not invent technologies or operational facts

evals.prompt: Make one Inkblot illustration about waiting. Keep it simple.
evals.expected_output: One Inkblot-first 16:9 illustration or final prompt with Inkblot as the main or only subject, no background plumbing, and no labels unless needed.
expectations: Chooses Inkblot-first because no real system was requested
Uses one Inkblot and no more than two essential props
Keeps every prop smaller and visually subordinate to Inkblot
Does not describe any prop as oversized
Leaves at least half the canvas empty
Defaults to no labels
Does not add a system diagram, plumbing scene, or truth ledger
